title: Chunking
content: Chunking is the splitting of a document into smaller passages so a retrieval system can index and return the relevant part.

meta.why: Retrieval systems do the splitting themselves, and Google states that breaking content into tiny pieces is not required for its AI features.
meta.example: A retrieval system divides a long returns policy into sections and returns the section about refund timing for a question about refunds.
meta.check: Read each section of a key page apart from the others and confirm the section names its subject and keeps its conditions beside the claim.
meta.limitation: Each system sets its own chunk size, and Google lists chunking among the tactics a site can ignore for Google Search.
